global_issues.title: US-China chip tariffs shift to case-by-case licensing
global_issues.note: Core facts are accurate — BIS did implement 25% tariffs plus case-by-case licensing for advanced nodes (H200, MI325X, etc.) with selective approvals and multi-week review cycles. However, the BIS final rule took effect January 15, 2026, not 'June 2026' as stated. This policy shift has been operational for six months and is not a recent development. The Reuters/Commerce Dept sourcing also conflicts with the Jan 2026 effective date.

global_issues.title: Iran Strait of Hormuz risk remains elevated
global_issues.note: Critically misleading framing. The briefing describes 'live missile drills' with tanker traffic continuing and +12% war-risk premiums since June 28. Reality: the US and Israel launched a full-scale air war against Iran on February 28, 2026 (Operation Epic Fury), killing Supreme Leader Khamenei. The IRGC fully blockaded the strait — tanker traffic dropped to near zero, not a minor premium increase. A ceasefire was reached ~April 7-8 after five-plus weeks of combat. As of July 2, Iran is warning all oil tankers to use 'approved routes or face a forceful response,' reflecting active post-war reopening negotiations, not routine drills. The strait closure is now a top-tier geopolitical ceasefire condition.

global_issues.title: DOJ AI partnership probe advances to depositions
global_issues.note: Active DOJ and FTC antitrust investigations into AI cloud partnerships involving Google, Microsoft-OpenAI, and others are confirmed by multiple sources including Congressional inquiries (Warren/Wyden) and FTC civil investigative demands. However, the specific claims — 'expanded civil discovery filed June 30,' GOOGL-META-MSFT cloud and model-sharing targets, executive depositions scheduled July 8-10 — could not be independently confirmed from available search results. Plausible as an extension of existing probes but the precise timeline and scope remain unverified.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's most serious failure is the Iran/Hormuz item: it describes contained missile drills with minor risk premium increases when the actual situation is a post-war active dispute — the US and Israel fought a multi-week air war against Iran starting February 28, 2026, the strait was nearly fully blocked, and as of July 2 Iran is issuing active routing threats to tankers. This is a material mischaracterization, not a nuance. Compounding this, the briefing omits the day's single most important market event: the June NFP print came in at 57K versus 115K expected, driving Nasdaq lower and shifting rate expectations — this affects nearly every stock in the watchlist. All stock price dates are also wrong (July 3 was a market holiday; these are July 2 closes).
